clue.text: Not speaking, not at first, having called back atmosphere in Italian region

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak

indicators.note: calling something back brings it the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: Someone silent in an Italian region, having phoned home, perhaps absorbing the local atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' strips D from DUMB to leave UMB; 'called back' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a landlocked region of central Italy, around Perugia.

clue.text: Motivational channel showing poor run hosted by club

indicators.note: the club plays host, holding the other letters within it

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
ill can mean poor, as in ill health
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A motivational TV channel airs a team's poor run of form at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motivational' is used in its literal sense: a millrace is the channel whose water sets the mill wheel in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the stream of water driving a mill wheel, so it is a channel supplying motive power.

clue.text: See 2
Endless strain suppressed by a supporter from Tunisia, say

indicators.note: the supporter holds down the other piece, so it sits inside

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: says the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to rick is to strain or sprain a joint

explanation.surface: A football fan from Tunisia trying to hide a nagging strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' is the verb sense, to sprain a joint; 'Endless' trims its final letter, and 'suppressed by' sinks what remains into the supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia lies in North Africa, so something from there is an example of African.

clue.text: He signals decline lots of people curtailed

parts.note: to flag is to tire or decline

indicators.note: a curtailed word has lost its tail, its last letter

parts.note: many means lots of people, as in 'many say so'

explanation.surface: A signaller waves people off as they flag, though the crowd has thinned.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagman is a railway or race worker who gives signals by waving flags.

clue.text: SF film? Activate SF agony with adaptation

indicators.note: adapting something reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A science-fiction movie stirs pain once adapted for the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic Voyage is the 1966 science-fiction film of a miniaturised submarine crew inside a human body.

clue.text: Army regulation requires something to fix bright light

parts.note: AR is the standard abbreviation for an Army Regulation
a clamp is a device for fixing things firmly in place

explanation.surface: Military rules demand that a bright lamp be bolted down securely.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces intense light from an electric arc between electrodes, used in searchlights and film studios.

clue.text: Male remains with it — it's something a club has?

parts.note: embers are the glowing remains of a fire
to be with it is to be fashionable, or hip

explanation.surface: A man's remains are kept, trendily, in a club's possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' is an idiom for fashionable, giving HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A club's membership is the body of people belonging to it, a thing every club possesses.

clue.text: Upturn in light swamping last of encircling dark

indicators.note: swamping engulfs something, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down entry an upturn reads the word from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: thin means light, as in thin fabric

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An improvement in the light overwhelms the last of the surrounding gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upturn in' reverses THIN to NIHT, which swamps G, the last letter of 'encircling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness, and dark is a noun for nightfall, as in 'after dark'.

clue.text: Voter, missing nothing, mostly put off regarding online voting?

indicators.note: says the letter that follows is left out of the word

parts.note: an elector is someone entitled to vote
O is the zero digit, nothing

indicators.note: says most of the phrase is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: on ice means put off or postponed, as in 'the plan is on ice'

explanation.surface: A voter, having nothing to say, is mostly deterred by the idea of voting online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing nothing' takes an O from ELECTOR; 'mostly' trims ON ICE to ONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting online is done by computer, so it is described as electronic, as in e-voting.

clue.text: "Wizard spread," Bunter finally expressed

indicators.note: to express is to press out, so a letter is squeezed out of the word

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a bread spread

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy of British comics, at last declares margarine a magical spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' squeezes R (the end of 'Bunter') out of MARGE. Billy Bunter is a gluttonous fictional British schoolboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mage is a literary word for a magician or sorcerer.

clue.text: Description of some molecular bonding providing energy in vacant lot, possibly

indicators.note: says one piece is placed inside the other
possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A chemist finds energy on an empty plot that might explain molecular bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges VACANT LOT, and 'in' places E within.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavalent describes an atom with a valency of eight, able to form eight chemical bonds.

clue.text: Ladies perhaps welcoming good company image

indicators.note: welcoming takes something in, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: the Ladies is a women's toilet, an example of a loo

explanation.surface: Women, perhaps, warmly greet a decent firm's public image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Ladies' is British for a women's public toilet; LOO is the informal word.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is the emblem or symbol that represents a company's brand.

clue.text: Starts to reject each request to Government — duplicated entries?

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: a petition is a formal written request to an authority such as government

explanation.surface: Officials begin rejecting every appeal to Government that has been submitted twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetition is the same thing occurring again, so duplicated entries are an instance of it.

clue.text: Have to get satellite in orbit to make progress

indicators.note: a satellite in orbit circles round something, so it wraps the other piece

parts.note: the moon is Earth's natural satellite
've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: A space agency must put a satellite into orbit to advance its programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The moon circles VE, the shortened 'have' as in I've.
explanation.definitionFit: To move on is to advance or go forward, an idiom for making progress.

clue.text: Records attempt to deliver ornamental textile

parts.note: tapes are recordings
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Archive tapes are an effort to produce a decorative fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven fabric with pictorial designs, hung as decoration.

clue.text: Intermittently rougher part of Germany

indicators.note: taking letters on and off, so every other letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A German industrial region is, at times, a little harsher.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is the major industrial district of western Germany, named after its river.

clue.text: Cathedral getting a lot of criticism in the home

parts.note: dome is an old word for a cathedral or great house, like Italian duomo

indicators.note: says most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: stick means harsh criticism, as in 'take some stick'

explanation.surface: A cathedral faces heavy criticism over its private affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts STICK to STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic means relating to the household, so happening at home.

clue.text: Drama and passion in plane possibly losing tail

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the other
the word drops its final letter

parts.note: the plane is a kind of tree
heat means passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: Drama and passion on an aircraft that may be losing its tail section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is not an aircraft but the plane tree; 'losing tail' drops its last letter, and 'in' puts the passion inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is the art of drama, plays performed on stage.

clue.text: Fine of low value for escape

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
light means slight or of little weight or worth

explanation.surface: A small fine imposed for breaking out of prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight is the act of fleeing, a synonym of escape, as in 'take flight'.

clue.text: France and America notice a source of irritation?

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
US is short for the United States of America
to spot is to notice

explanation.surface: France and America spot something irritating in each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is a fussy person who frets over trifles, someone who tends to annoy others.

clue.text: Pay for ultimate in mulch, put amongst flourishing roses — equine source?

indicators.note: says these pieces are placed within the other letters
flourishing roses are tossed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to hire is to pay for the use of something

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener pays for manure to spread among flourishing roses, sourced from horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourishing' rearranges the roses into S…ORSE around the payment and the last letter of 'mulch'. A shire horse is a British heavy draught breed, a natural source of manure for roses.
explanation.definitionFit: A shire horse is a large draught breed, and as a horse it is a source of horse manure for gardens.

clue.text: Feel unwell aboard boat trips at sea?

indicators.note: being aboard a vessel puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: Passengers feeling seasick on a boat during trips at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sail is a voyage on a boat, so sails are journeys on water.

clue.text: Error with nautical speed? Tug will put paid to it

definitions.text: Tug will put paid to it

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake
a knot is a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile per hour

explanation.surface: A navigation error about speed at sea, which a tugboat will fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tug' is a pull on a rope, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipknot is a knot that comes undone with one pull on the free end.

clue.text: See 21
Brief note left incomplete

indicators.note: says the word is left unfinished, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a minim is a musical note of two beats

explanation.surface: A short message has been left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini means small or short, as in a mini-break, so it fits brief.

clue.text: Gym equipment? Cargo boat has old stock on hand

parts.note: a tramp is a cargo ship with no fixed route
a line is a range of goods a shop keeps in stock

explanation.surface: A cargo vessel carries old stock available for gym fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung canvas for bouncing, used as gymnastics apparatus.

clue.text: True crime about to involve church

indicators.note: involving something wraps it in, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: sin means a wrong or crime
re means about, concerning
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A genuine crime is about to drag in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and honest, a sense of true as in a true friend.

clue.text: Young child returned cuddling a cat or dog, say, or rabbit

indicators.note: cuddling holds something close inside
something returned comes back the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a baby is sometimes called 'it'
cats and dogs are examples of pets

explanation.surface: A toddler comes back hugging the family pet, a cat, dog or rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IT into TI, which cuddles A PET.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapeti is a South American wild rabbit species, the Brazilian cottontail.
